source_evidence: Rising interest rates will make newly issued bonds more appealing to investors because the newer bonds will have a higher rate of interest than older ones.
question: Misconception: If market interest rates rise, an older bond’s value rises too because its interest payments stay the same.
answer: Correction: Rising rates can make newly issued bonds more appealing because they offer higher interest. An older bond with a lower rate may need to be sold at a discount. If held to maturity, the investor receives the face value plus interest.
